question: Why do two standard series disagree by about seven points on American unemployment in 1936?
answer: Because of how relief workers are counted. Stanley Lebergott's series treats people on federal work programmes such as the WPA as unemployed and gives about 17%; Michael Darby counted them as employed and got about 10%. Private jobs are identical in both. Whether the New Deal recovery looks fast or slow turns on one column.
move: Before comparing two figures, check who each one counts as what.
ask: Before I compare two numbers this week, do I know who each one counts and who it leaves out?
